content:
Let  

\[
A=(0,0),\qquad E=(20,0)
\]

because \(AE=20\) and \(\angle A=\angle E =90^{\circ}\).
Since the interior of the pentagon lies on the same side of \(AE\) as
\(B,C,D\), the sides \(AB\) and \(DE\) are vertical.

\[
B=(0,b),\qquad D=(20,d),\qquad b=AB,\;d=DE .
\]

---

### Using the given angles at \(B\) and \(D\)

At \(B\) the interior angle between the sides \(BA\) (downward) and
\(BC\) is \(45^{\circ}\); hence \(BC\) makes an angle of \(45^{\circ}\)
with the vertical, i.e. it is directed down‑right with slope \(-1\).

\[
BC = 14\sqrt2\Longrightarrow
\overrightarrow{BC} = (14,-14),
\]

so  

\[
C = B+\overrightarrow{BC}= (14,\;b-14).
\]

At \(D\) the interior angle between \(DC\) (down‑left) and \(DE\) (down)
is also \(45^{\circ}\). Consequently  

\[
\overrightarrow{DC}=(-k,-k)
\]

for some \(k>0\).  Since \(C\) is already known,

\[
(20-k,\;d-k)=(14,\;b-14)\Longrightarrow k=6,\quad d=b-8 .
\]

Thus  

\[
D=(20,\;b-8),\qquad DE = d = b-8 .
\]

The condition \(DE<AB\) is automatically satisfied (\(b-8<b\)) and
\(b>14\) guarantees that the points lie above \(AE\).

---

### Area of the pentagon

Using the vertices in order \(A(0,0),B(0,b),C(14,b-14),D(20,b-8),E(20,0)\)
and the shoelace formula,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Area} &=\frac12\bigl|
0\cdot b+0\cdot(b-14)+14\cdot(b-8)+20\cdot0+20\cdot0 \\
&\qquad -\bigl(0\cdot0+b\cdot14+(b-14)\cdot20+(b-8)\cdot20+0\cdot0\bigr)
\bigr| \\[2mm]
&=\frac12\bigl|14(b-8)-(54b-440)\bigr|
     =\frac12\bigl|-40b+328\bigr|
     =20b-164 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence  

\[
\boxed{\text{Area}=20b-164 }.
\]

---

### Condition on the area

The problem requires the area to be an integer multiple of \(16\):

\[
20b-164 \equiv 0 \pmod{16}\Longrightarrow 4b-164 \equiv 0 \pmod{16}
\Longrightarrow 4b\equiv 4 \pmod{16}
\Longrightarrow b\equiv 1 \pmod{4}.
\]

Thus \(AB=b\) must be an integer congruent to \(1\) modulo \(4\).

---

### Counting admissible values of \(AB\)

\[
\begin{cases}
b\equiv 1\pmod 4,\\[2pt]
b>14\;( \text{so } b\ge 17),\\[2pt]
b<2026 .
\end{cases}
\]

Numbers of the form \(b=4k+1\) satisfy \(4k+1\ge 17\Rightarrow k\ge 4\)
and \(4k+1\le 2025\Rightarrow k\le 506\).

Hence \(k\) can be any integer from \(4\) through \(506\), a total of  

\[
506-4+1 = 503
\]

possibilities.

\[
\boxed{503}
\]
